chapter.title: Authenticated-control report truth (PROOFS-a)

pitfalls.failure: An API report is mistaken for a rendered browser journey
pitfalls.recovery: Require actual DOM observations and no skipped claims before admitting browser completeness

frontier: One original case remains: full authenticated Builder navigation/actions/screenshot journey against the running product. Controlled composition and DOM classifier documents do not prove that product journey or live provider execution.
guidance: Pure startup composition exercises live route projection, redacted diagnostics and refusal of forged completeness.
An explicit username/password skips credential file fallback; startup never loads saved credentials.

contracts.claim: Live Builder URLs retain origin and mission parameters, force Builder mode, remove fixture/preview flags and discard fragments.
Every emitted diagnostic removes explicit and labeled credentials, collapses whitespace and bounds text to 1200 characters.
Report status and counters equal measured, failed and skipped observations; missing or duplicate browser claim identities are refused.
API-only reports emit every DOM claim as skipped, unmeasured and without a pass; they never claim complete browser proof.
Every provider DOM measurement distinguishes visible admission/quota semantics and explicit admitted/blocked lanes from explanatory prose.
Every Hermes DOM measurement requires a visible strip, literal verified marker and explicit proven receipt text; pending or absent strips never pass.
The production CLI parses and exposes an explicit --with-browser option; DOM classification uses actual installed Chromium observations.
A failed browser measurement preserves completed login observations and leaves all unobserved DOM claims skipped; partial screenshots never become positive DOM proof.
